nodes.description: Ciliary INPP5E converts PI(4,5)P2 to PI4P, keeping the ciliary membrane PI4P-rich. When INPP5E is absent, PI(4,5)P2 accumulates and recruits TULP3 together with the Hedgehog-repressing receptor GPR161 into the cilium, raising ciliary cAMP.

evidence.reference_title: Modulation of Ciliary Phosphoinositide Content Regulates Trafficking and Sonic Hedgehog Signaling Output.
evidence.snippet: Our results reveal the link between ciliary regulation of phosphoinositides by INPP5E and Shh regulation via ciliary trafficking of TULP3/Gpr161 and also provide mechanistic insight into ciliary alterations found in Joubert and MORM syndromes resulting from INPP5E mutations.

nodes.description: Farnesylated INPP5E is carried to the cilium by the prenyl-binding protein PDE6D, released inside the cilium by ARL3-GTP, and retained with the help of ARL13B. Without its farnesylated C terminus the truncated MORM protein cannot use this route and fails to accumulate in the ciliary membrane. The same targeting failure is produced from the carrier side by a homozygous PDE6D splice variant in Joubert syndrome. The conformance target is the module's ciliary-gating node; the MORM defect is in cargo targeting rather than in basal-body or transition-zone structure, so the fit is partial.

nodes.description: Both MORM alleles are nonsense variants in the terminal exon of INPP5E that delete the last residues of the protein, including the CaaX box whose cysteine (Cys644) is farnesylated. Unlike the Joubert syndrome 1 variants, which cluster in the phosphatase domain and abolish catalysis, the MORM truncations leave the phosphatase domain intact; ClinGen's curation records that the MORM variants lose membrane localisation while retaining enzymatic activity.

nodes.description: Loss of ciliary INPP5E does not prevent cilium assembly but destabilises pre-existing cilia after growth-factor stimulation, through unopposed ciliary PDGFR-alpha and PI3K signalling; blocking either restores stability in Inpp5e-deficient cells.

nodes.description: Ciliary GPR161 and raised cAMP hold the Hedgehog pathway in its repressed state, lowering Gli1 output.
